U1.title: The Amazing Octopus
U1.content:
Among the many amazing animals in the world, few are as strange and unusual as the octopus. There are around 300 different kinds of octopuses, and they come in all sizes! The smallest is only around 2.5 centimetres long, but some octopuses can grow up to more than five metres long. There was even an octopus over nine metres long!

The octopus's body is very interesting. All octopuses have eight arms. Their brain is not just in their head, but also in their arms! This helps them to think about and do more than one thing at once. Octopuses can also fit into small places because they do not have any bones! And did you know that octopuses have three hearts? These hearts work with different parts of the body.

Octopuses can also do many amazing things. Most of them can change their colour and shape to look like plants or other sea animals, and they can also make ink. They keep it inside a very small bag in their body. When they produce ink, the ink makes it hard for other animals to see them. This helps the octopuses to get away fast. What's more, when an octopus loses an arm, it can grow it back!

Studying amazing animals like the octopus is important because we can learn a lot from them. But they also show us how wonderful nature is and why it is important to protect it.

U1.title: Zookeeper for a Day
U1.content:
Do you love animals?
Why not join us in a school trip to the zoo this Saturday? It can help you know about animals well.

You'll have lots of fun being a zookeeper!
Time: 10:30 a.m. — 2:30 p.m.
Who: Students in Grade 6 and Grade 7
What to bring:
- A yellow hat
- A camera (照相机) or a phone
- Some water and food

What to do:
- Give food to koalas
- Do some cleaning for pandas
- Take photos with cute birds
- Watch an elephant show

We need to take the bus to the zoo, so we have to meet at school before 9:30 a.m.

U1.title: A Special Class in the Zoo
U1.content:
Today we have a special class in the zoo. Our teacher Miss Green asks us to look at different animals and write something about them.

There are many people in the zoo. Peter, Jenny and I are watching the monkeys. The monkeys are cute and clever, but they are not quiet! They like to jump around and make noise.

"What can we write about these monkeys?" Jenny asks.

Peter is very smart. He asks Jenny to give these monkeys some bananas. Then all the monkeys come to them.

All of us are happy to have the class in the zoo.

U1.title: Protecting Milu Deer
U1.content:
Yu Xiaopeng works at a nature reserve in Yancheng, Jiangsu. His work is domesticating the milu deer.

Each morning, Yu gets up early and walks around with a notebook. He feeds the milu deer and writes down how much water and food they have for each day. He looks after them well to make sure they are healthy. For Yu, the milu deer are like his children.

Yu knows the milu deer well. He can tell where they like to go and what they love to eat. Yu thinks there could be more visitors. "They can get close to the cute animals and learn more about them," Yu said. "It can also help protect the milu deer."

The milu deer are a symbol of good luck in China. But they got into great danger in the 1980s because there were not many of them at that time. In 1986, the reserve welcomed 39 milu deer from the UK. Thanks to people like Yu, there are over 8,000 milu deer in it now. Yu wants to keep doing the job and ask more people to protect the milu deer.

U1.title: How to Take Care of Pets
U1.content:
Taking care of a pet is hard work. There are a lot of things for you to do.

We should feed the pets at the right time. They need healthy and nutritious food to help them grow healthy and strong. They also need to drink plenty of clean, fresh water.

All of the pets need a safe place. It is their home. It can be a house with a backyard or a cage. But we must know different animals require different space in size.

Pets like dogs need plenty of exercise each day. In many cases, walking 1.6 kilometres a day with your dog can help it get the exercise it needs. Cats need exercise too. And a fifteen- to twenty-minute-long walk is a good starting point.

Just like humans, pets need visits to the vet to make sure that they're in great health. Taking your pet dog to visit the vet once a year is all right. Older dogs may need more visits to the vet.

U1.title: The Life of Pandas
U1.content:
Although the panda is one of the best-known, best-loved and cutest animals in the world, it lives a solitary life. Pandas once lived in a few parts of Asia, including Vietnam and Burma, but now they live only in some parts of China.

Pandas spend about 12 hours every day eating. They mainly eat bamboo. And they always travel between different places to find fresh bamboo. Also, they eat fruit, other plants and some fish.

Pandas usually live in cold and wet places. Their black-and-white coats keep them warm.

Pandas are very good at climbing. If people or animals run after them, they will climb up the nearest tree very quickly. Their good hearing also helps them to avoid animals who want to eat them.

There are about 1,900 wild pandas left in China. Their main problem is that their living places are becoming smaller and smaller. China has realized this problem and is trying her best to do things for pandas. Now, China has set up some special places which are big enough for pandas to live in.

U1.title: The Ugliest Fish in the World
U1.content:
Most people don't know about blobfish. They're the world's ugliest fish.

Blobfish live in the sea near Australia and New Zealand. For most of time, they stay in the water between 600 to 1,200 metres deep. When some little fish swim past them, they try to catch them for food. They can grow to 30 cm long. They have very large heads, small bodies and thin tails. They look like a large jelly. So they get their name.

People don't eat blobfish, because they are not good for people to eat. But fishermen kill thousands of them each year when they catch other fish in the sea. Scientists are worried that this will put the blobfish on the list of animals in danger.
